nodes.description: Abnormal shaping of the external ear produces the cleft or absent lobule and dysplastic, protruding pinnae; hearing is typically normal. HMX1 is expressed in branchial arch mesenchyme, from which the pinna develops. In the dumbo rat, deletion of a distant enhancer removes Hmx1 only from neural-crest-derived craniofacial mesenchyme and still produces the ear malformation, indicating that mesenchymal HMX1 is what the pinna requires; in human disease the coding alleles remove HMX1 in all tissues. Only the dysplastic pinna phenotype is linked, because no cited source states which specific lobule or helix defect follows from the morphogenesis defect.

nodes.description: HMX1 dimerizes through its SD1 domain and homeodomain, needs the homeodomain for nuclear localization, and represses EPHA6, a retinal axon-guidance gene; in zebrafish it also regulates uhrf1 in the cranial region. How dysregulation of these targets produces the human eye and ear malformations has not been shown, so this node has no downstream edge.

nodes.description: Biallelic HMX1 variants remove or disable the homeodomain of this transcription factor. The original family carries a homozygous 26-nucleotide deletion in exon 1 that truncates the protein before the homeodomain; later families carry a homozygous homeodomain missense (p.Gln217Pro) that is expressed but functionally impaired, and homozygous nonsense or frameshift alleles (p.Glu163*, p.Ala85Argfs*53).

nodes.description: A regulatory allele that removes Hmx1 expression from neural-crest-derived craniofacial mesenchyme while sparing retinal expression; neonates show ear and eye phenotypes similar to dumbo mice. Because the lesion is noncoding, it models HMX1 regulatory ear malformation more closely than the human coding alleles of oculoauricular syndrome.

In zebrafish, hmx1 is expressed in the nasal retina and lens, and its knockdown delays cell-cycle exit of retinal progenitors, retards retinal differentiation, increases cell death and produces a small eye.

nodes.description: Developmental malformation of the anterior segment and lens, and incomplete closure of the optic fissure, produce anterior segment dysgenesis, congenital cataract and colobomas. The authors of the second family's report propose an HMX1 role in the lens and retina developmental pathway and in the optic fissure closure gene network; the cellular mechanism is not established. Microcornea and posterior synechiae are not linked from this node because no cited source states the link directly; the chorioretinal and optic disc colobomas are linked by the same optic fissure closure proposal as the iris coloboma.

nodes.description: Electroretinography first shows generalized rod more than cone dysfunction, followed by rapid loss of both rod and cone function, giving a progressive rod-cone dystrophy that begins in infancy. Abnormalities of the retinal pigment epithelium are also described. Whether this degeneration is a consequence of the developmental retinal defect or a separate requirement for HMX1 in mature photoreceptors is not known.
